sentences.l: “He works in the garden: the strange fellow has been at the festival too and only came back yesterday evening;
sentences.i: “He is working in the garden; the odd fellow was at the festival too and only came back yesterday evening;
sentences.n: “der Kautz” is properly a small owl, and of a person it means an odd character, a queer fellow — said here with affection. “wunderlich” is strange, odd. “erst” means “only, not until.”

sentences.t: er hat auch meinen Kindern drei goldene Äpfel gezeigt, die er gewonnen hat.“
sentences.l: he has also shown my children three golden apples that he has won.”
sentences.i: he has even shown my children three golden apples that he won.”
sentences.n: The gardener has no idea what he is saying: the three apples are the proof the king has been hunting. German keeps the perfect where English would use a simple past.

sentences.t: Der König ließ ihn vor sich fordern, und er erschien und hatte wieder sein Hütchen auf dem Kopf.
sentences.l: The king had him summoned before him, and he appeared and had his little-cap on his head again.
sentences.i: The king had him summoned before him, and he appeared with his little cap on his head again.
sentences.n: “fordern” here is to summon, not to demand: “vor sich fordern lassen” is to have someone called into one’s presence. The cap is still on — he does not give himself away even now.

sentences.t: Aber die Königstochter gieng auf ihn zu und nahm es ihm ab, und da fielen seine goldenen Haare über die Schultern, und er war so schön, daß alle erstaunten.
sentences.l: But the king’s-daughter went up to him and took it off him, and then his golden hair fell over his shoulders, and he was so beautiful that all were astonished.
sentences.i: But the king’s daughter went up to him and took it off him, and his golden hair fell down over his shoulders, and he was so beautiful that they were all astonished.
sentences.n: “auf jemanden zugehen” is separable, to walk up to someone. “nahm es ihm ab” has the dative of the person again: took it from him. She is the one who uncovers him, as she tried to do three times in the garden.

sentences.t: „Bist du der Ritter gewesen, der jeden Tag zu dem Fest gekommen ist, immer in einer andern Farbe, und der die drei goldenen Äpfel gefangen hat?“ fragte der König.
sentences.l: “Have you been the knight who came to the festival every day, always in a different colour, and who caught the three golden apples?” asked the king.
sentences.i: “Were you the knight who came to the festival every day, always in a different colour, and who caught the three golden apples?” asked the king.
sentences.n: German’s perfect “bist du … gewesen” is its ordinary past in speech, where English says “were you.” “die Farbe” is the colour of each day’s armour: red, white, black.

sentences.t: „Ja“ antwortete er, „und da sind die Äpfel,“ holte sie aus seiner Tasche und reichte sie dem König.
sentences.l: “Yes” answered he, “and there are the apples,” fetched them out of his pocket and handed them to the king.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he answered, “and here are the apples” — and he took them out of his pocket and handed them to the king.
sentences.n: The sentence changes course in the middle: the speech breaks off and the narration runs on with no new subject named, so the idiomatic line supplies “and he.” “da sind” is “there are” in the sense of “here they are.”

sentences.t: „Wenn ihr noch mehr Beweise verlangt, so könnt ihr die Wunde sehen, die mir eure Leute geschlagen haben, als sie mich verfolgten.
sentences.l: “If you demand still more proofs, then you can see the wound that your people struck me when they pursued me.
sentences.i: “If you ask for further proof, you can see the wound your men dealt me when they pursued me.
sentences.n: He says “ihr” to the king — the old respectful plural, like French vous — while the king says “du” to him. “Beweise” is the plural noun, proofs, not a form of beweisen. “eine Wunde schlagen” is to deal a wound, with the dative of the person wounded.

sentences.t: Aber ich bin auch der Ritter, der euch zum Sieg über die Feinde geholfen hat.“
sentences.l: But I am also the knight who helped you to the victory over the enemy.”
sentences.i: And I am also the knight who helped you to the victory over the enemy.”
sentences.n: “helfen” takes the dative — “der euch geholfen hat” — and “zum Sieg helfen” is to help someone to a victory.

sentences.t: „Wenn du solche Thaten verrichten kannst, so bist du kein Gärtnerjunge: sage mir, wer ist dein Vater?“
sentences.l: “If you can perform such deeds, then you are no gardener’s-boy: tell me, who is your father?”
sentences.i: “If you can perform such deeds, you are no gardener’s boy; tell me, who is your father?”
sentences.n: “Thaten” is the plural of die That (the 1857 spelling of Tat), deeds — not a form of thun, which it resembles. “verrichten” is to perform, carry out. The king’s “so bist du” is the “then” of a conclusion drawn on the spot.

sentences.t: „Mein Vater ist ein mächtiger König und Goldes habe ich die Fülle und so viel ich nur verlange.“
sentences.l: “My father is a mighty king, and of gold I have abundance and as much as I ever demand.”
sentences.i: “My father is a mighty king, and I have gold in plenty, as much as I care to ask for.”
sentences.n: “Goldes” is an old genitive, of gold, standing before its noun: “Goldes habe ich die Fülle,” of gold I have abundance. What he says is true twice over — his own father is a king, and Eisenhans has promised him all he asks.

sentences.t: „Ich sehe wohl,“ sprach der König, „ich bin dir Dank schuldig, kann ich dir etwas zu Gefallen thun?“
sentences.l: “I see well,” spoke the king, “I am owing you thanks, can I do you something as a favour?”
sentences.i: “I see it well,” said the king; “I am in your debt — can I do you some favour?”
sentences.n: “Dank schuldig sein” is to owe thanks, with the dative of the person. “jemandem etwas zu Gefallen thun” is to do someone a favour: Gefallen is a noun here, a kindness, not a form of fallen.

sentences.t: „Ja“ antwortete er, „das könnt ihr wohl, gebt mir eure Tochter zur Frau.“
sentences.l: “Yes” answered he, “that you can well, give me your daughter to wife.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he answered, “that you can indeed: give me your daughter to wife.”
sentences.n: “jemandem zur Frau geben” is the formula for giving a woman in marriage. He keeps the respectful “ihr” to the king even while asking this.

sentences.t: Da lachte die Jungfrau und sprach „der macht keine Umstände, aber ich habe schon an seinen goldenen Haaren gesehen daß er kein Gärtnerjunge ist:“
sentences.l: Then the maiden laughed and spoke “that one makes no ado, but I have seen already by his golden hair that he is no gardener’s-boy:”
sentences.i: Then the maiden laughed and said, “He stands on no ceremony — but I saw long ago by his golden hair that he is no gardener’s boy:”
sentences.n: “der” at the head is the demonstrative — that one, he there — a familiar and half-amused way of naming him. “keine Umstände machen” is to make no fuss, to stand on no ceremony. “an etwas sehen” is to tell by something.

sentences.t: gieng dann hin und küßte ihn.
sentences.l: [she] then went over and kissed him.
sentences.i: and then she went over and kissed him.
sentences.n: The clause has no subject: German drops “sie” after the speech and simply carries on, so the literal supplies [she] in square brackets. “hingehen” is separable.

sentences.t: Zu der Vermählung kam sein Vater und seine Mutter und waren in großer Freude, denn sie hatten schon alle Hoffnung aufgegeben ihren lieben Sohn wieder zu sehen.
sentences.l: To the marriage came his father and his mother and were in great joy, for they had already given up all hope of seeing their dear son again.
sentences.i: His father and his mother came to the wedding and were in great joy, for they had long given up all hope of seeing their dear son again.
sentences.n: The verb agrees with the first subject alone — “kam sein Vater und seine Mutter” — which German allows and English does not. “die Hoffnung aufgeben” is to give up hope. Nothing has been said of them since the second block; the tale gathers them up in one line.

sentences.t: Und als sie an der Hochzeitstafel saßen, da schwieg auf einmal die Musik, die Thüren giengen auf und ein stolzer König trat herein mit großem Gefolge.
sentences.l: And as they sat at the wedding-table, then all at once the music fell silent, the doors went open and a proud king stepped in with a great retinue.
sentences.i: And as they sat at the wedding table, all at once the music fell silent, the doors opened, and a proud king stepped in with a great retinue.
sentences.n: “schweigen” is to fall silent, said here of the music itself. “auf einmal” is all at once. “stolz” of a person is proud in the sense of splendid, imposing — the same word used of the chestnut horse.

sentences.t: Er gieng auf den Jüngling zu, umarmte ihn und sprach „ich bin der Eisenhans, und war in einen wilden Mann verwünscht, aber du hast mich erlöst.
sentences.l: He went up to the youth, embraced him and spoke “I am the Eisenhans, and was cursed into a wild man, but you have redeemed me.
sentences.i: He went up to the youth, embraced him and said, “I am Eisenhans, and I was cursed into the shape of a wild man, but you have set me free.
sentences.n: “in etwas verwünschen” is to curse someone into another shape — the ordinary machinery of enchantment in these tales, and the plain statement that the wild man was never a savage but a king under a spell. “erlösen” is to redeem, to release from a spell. The German says “der Eisenhans,” with the article, as one names a figure everybody knows.

sentences.t: Alle Schätze, die ich besitze, die sollen dein Eigenthum sein.“
sentences.l: All treasures that I possess, they shall be your property.”
sentences.i: All the treasures that I possess shall be your own.”
sentences.n: The fronted phrase is taken up again by “die” — the same pattern as the tale’s very first sentence, still working in its last. “Eigenthum” is the 1857 spelling of Eigentum. He keeps, at the end, the promise he made in the forest to the boy who freed him.

glossary.acht: acht — eight (the number; ein Sohn von acht Jahren); also die Acht — heed (acht haben: to take care)
glossary.aufgegeben: aufgeben — given up (past part.; die Hoffnung aufgeben: to give up hope)
glossary.ausgezogen: ausziehen — marched out (past part. with sein; in den Krieg ausziehen: to march out to war; elsewhere: to take off, to strip)
glossary.band: binden — bound, tied (3rd sg. past; band zusammen: tied together)
glossary.bedenken: das Bedenken — misgiving, scruple (alles Bedenken in den Wind schlagen: to throw all scruples to the wind)
glossary.begab: sich begeben — betook himself, made his way (3rd sg. past)
glossary.behielt: aufbehalten — kept on (3rd sg. past; the particle waits at the end: behielt … auf; plain behalten: to keep)
glossary.beweise: der Beweis — proofs (pl. Beweise; noch mehr Beweise verlangen: to ask for further proof)
glossary.binde: aufbinden — untie, unbind (imperative sg.; the particle waits at the end: binde … auf)
glossary.brach: abbrechen — broke off, picked (3rd sg. past; the particle waits at the end: brach … ab; plain brechen: to break)
glossary.bring: bringen — bring (imperative sg.; bring mir einen Blumenstrauß: bring me a bunch of flowers)
glossary.deiner: dein — your (gen./dat. fem.; deiner Mutter: of your mother)
glossary.eins: eins — one, one thing (neuter; suche dir eins: find yourself one)
glossary.ergehen: ergehen — über sich ergehen lassen: to let something pass over one, to put up with it
glossary.fuchs: der Fuchs — a chestnut horse (a horse of fox-red coat; otherwise: fox)
glossary.gefallen: gefallen — to please (with dative); der Gefallen — a favour (jemandem etwas zu Gefallen thun); also fallen — fallen (in battle)
glossary.hacken: hacken — to hoe, to break ground with a hoe (infinitive)
glossary.hauen: hauen — to strike, to cut at (auf jemanden hauen: to strike at someone with a blade; elsewhere: to hew, to chop)
glossary.hieß: heißen — bade, told (to do) (3rd sg. past with a bare infinitive: hieß ihn tragen, bade him carry; elsewhere: was called)
glossary.hingehen: hingehen — to pass, to be let go (es mag hingehen: let it pass; elsewhere: to go there)
glossary.hole: holen — fetch (imperative sg.; hole andere: fetch others)
glossary.ja: ja — yes (in answer); as a particle: indeed, after all
glossary.junge: der Junge — boy, lad (masc. noun; also jung — young, inflected)
glossary.jungen: der Junge — boy, lad (acc./dat. sg.; nach seinem Jungen: after his boy)
glossary.kehren: kehren — to sweep (die Asche zusammen kehren); with zurück: to return
glossary.kehrte: kehren — turned (3rd sg. past; kehrte um: turned back; zurück kehrte: returned)
glossary.macht: die Macht — power, might (fem. noun); also machen — makes (3rd sg.)
glossary.nachsehen: nachsehen — to overlook, to let someone off (infinitive, with the dative of the person: dirs nachsehen; elsewhere: to look and see)
glossary.roß: das Roß — steed, war-horse (1857 spelling of Ross)
glossary.sage: sagen — (I) say (1st sg. present; was ich dir sage: what I tell you)
glossary.setzte: setzen — set, placed (3rd sg. past; setzte ihn auf seinen Nacken: set him on his neck; sich setzen: to sit down; setzte … auf: put on; setzte sich auf: mounted)
glossary.spitze: die Spitze — point, tip (mit der Spitze des Schwerts: with the point of the sword)
glossary.stechen: stechen — to thrust, to stab (with the point of a weapon; hauen und stechen: to cut and thrust)
glossary.stricken: der Strick — ropes, cords (dat. pl. Stricken; mit Stricken binden: to bind with ropes)
glossary.suche: suchen — seek, pick out (imperative sg.; suche … aus is aussuchen, to pick out; suche dir eins: find yourself one)
glossary.thaten: die That — deeds (pl. Thaten; 1857 spelling of Tat)
glossary.verbot: verbieten — forbade (3rd sg. past; also das Verbot: a prohibition)
glossary.verfolgt: verfolgen — pursued (past part.; er hat die Feinde verfolgt)
glossary.verlangst: verlangen — (you) demand, ask for (2nd sg. present; was verlangst du?: what do you ask?)
glossary.verlangt: verlangen — (you) demand, ask for (2nd pl. present; wenn ihr verlangt)
glossary.volk: das Volk — people, folk; here the king’s fighting men
glossary.wagen: wagen — to dare, to venture (infinitive; sich in den Wald wagen: to venture into the forest)
glossary.weh: weh — sore, painful (weh thun, with the dative of the person: to hurt someone; also das Weh, woe)
glossary.weichen: weichen — to give way, to fall back (infinitive)
glossary.weiß: wissen — (I) know (1st sg. present; von Furcht weiß ich nichts); also weiß — white
glossary.wetter: das Wetter — weather; also a storm (fuhr wie ein Wetter: swept like a storm)
glossary.widerstand: der Widerstand — resistance (Widerstand leisten: to offer resistance)
glossary.wild: das Wild — game, wild animals (collective, n.; also wild — wild, adj.)
glossary.wohlgefallen: das Wohlgefallen — liking, pleasure (Wohlgefallen an jemandem haben: to take a liking to someone)
glossary.wozu: wozu — for what, to what end (wozu brauchen: what to use someone for)
